objective: Scouting pass (documentation). Is unsolvability of the signed no-lone law ({0,2,3}; {0,1,3} by complement) on cubic systems recognisable in polynomial time? A first probe found unsolvable signings only on graphs where not-all-equal has none (n = 6, 7). Census of small cubic graphs (all signings modulo point switching), the structure of unsolvable instances (minimal ones, relation to Pfaffian graphs), the literature on bounded-occurrence Boolean constraint satisfaction (Feder 2001; Dalmau and Ford 2003; Kazda, Kolmogorov and Rolinek), and either a characterisation or a hardness argument. Discriminator: a polynomial test that matches the census, or a reduction.
status: Closed (documentation, scouting): the signed Fibonacci law is NP-complete on cubic systems (constant gadget, equality lines, Schaefer); not-all-equal gadgets are rigid (nothing, everything, itself) up to 5 internal points; 1/3 hardness, 2/3 rigidity
title: Lane C: the signed Fibonacci law
